A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Force Field research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original prediction, planning, force-reconstruction, ablation, and robustness results on I-PHYRE, N-body, and PHYRE.

after.justification: v5 retains original experiments on all three benchmarks and reports revised N-body results and additional baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The architecture, loss, interaction graphs, and planning procedures are retained. However, v5 explicitly divides predicted force by known mass, whereas v4 describes absorbing mass into the learned field. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the implemented procedure or clarifies its parameterization.

E1.justification: The three principal benchmarks and their standard scenarios remain. v5 removes the additional N-body training-noise scenarios and I-PHYRE evaluation using states extracted from RGB images through OpenCV, reducing coverage of imperfect inputs.

E2.justification: v5 adds SEGNO to the I-PHYRE and N-body prediction comparisons and adds EGNN and GraphODE on N-body. GCN remains in the N-body appendix comparison, but its I-PHYRE comparison disappears. Planning comparators, including GPT-4o, are retained.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes the stated step size for the without-ODE control from 1e-3 to 5e-3; this does not establish that it was rerun. The Euler sweep drops 1e-2 and 5e-2, while evaluation of the already-present adaptive solver expands to training and longer-horizon prediction. Standard dataset splits, budgets, and metrics remain.

E4.justification: v5 removes both robustness studies from v4 Appendix D: N-body training noise and I-PHYRE imperfect perception. It also revises the integration-precision ablation and expands reporting for adaptive integration. Controlled force-response analyses and prediction-failure case studies remain, so these are substantive changes to the analysis suite rather than appendix relocations.

E5.justification: Both versions retain SEM reporting, the same planning-trial information, and three repetitions for planning-time measurements. Additional rows and revised uncertainty values do not introduce a different statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: N-body results change substantially: Table 1 reports NFF short-horizon within-scenario RMSE of 0.139 in v4 versus 0.097 in v5, and cross-scenario RMSE of 1.090 versus 1.226. These are revised reported scores, without assuming identical solver settings. New SEGNO rows show lower short-horizon errors than NFF, and integration results switch the best cross-scenario solver from Heun3 to Euler. Noise-result entries disappear; planning results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the formal force-to-acceleration relationship: Equations (2) and (4) explicitly use F/m, accompanied by a distinction between known mass and implicitly learned mass-normalized forces. No theorem or proof is added, and the remaining mathematical development and metric definitions are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about few-shot force learning, generalization, and planning remain. The introduction extends the superiority claim to EGNN and SEGNO, while the abstract and conclusion more explicitly delimit the demonstrated results to abstract physical-reasoning tasks.

C2.justification: The discussion replaces proposed social and biological applications with an explicit acknowledgment that real-world transfer remains unexplored and a proposed foundation-model perception interface. The noisy-state robustness interpretation disappears. Euler is now justified partly by superior cross-scenario accuracy, whereas v4 chose it despite Heun3's accuracy advantage.

D1.justification: v5 newly states that encoded states are fed directly into SlotFormer for the state-based comparisons; this disclosure does not establish an input-protocol change. OpenCV extraction details disappear with the perception experiment. Hardware, architecture and training hyperparameters, the project link, and the promise of future code/data availability are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against equivariant GNNs, graph ODEs, rigid/deformable simulators, and slot-based models. Appendix A adds discussions of planning and physics-aware video generation while retaining relocated physics-informed work. Numerous corresponding citations are added, and the social/biological-force references are removed.

P1.justification: v5 reorganizes related work between Section 2 and Appendix A, revises the mass explanation and discussion, adds a reproducibility statement, removes the NeurIPS checklist, and updates author information. The principal section sequence and most method, experimental, and retained appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes branch/trunk labeling, and Figure 2 gains time labels, a vector legend, and an expanded caption. Table 4 changes its integration columns; a baseline table is added and two noise tables are removed. The ICLR format changes headers and float placement, while the retained result figures preserve their visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v5 offers broader baseline comparisons, stronger research context, and clearer applicability limits. However, it removes two robustness studies and introduces inconsistencies between revised results and retained descriptions: Section 4.3 still claims superiority across all metrics despite SEGNO's lower short-horizon errors, and Table A2 still favors Heun3 in its caption although Euler has the best cross-scenario score. These benefits coexist with reduced robustness evidence and reporting problems, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
